clue.text: Saluting cartoon, awfully well done

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone salutes a cartoon and offers a terribly hearty well done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges SALUTING CARTOON, all fifteen letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying well done is offering praise, the same as an exclamation of congratulation.

clue.text: Spots on TV: one, a lecturer fills for Welsh region

indicators.note: the lecturer word fills a gap in the chain of other pieces, so it goes inside

parts.note: snow is the speckled interference seen on a badly tuned television
the Roman numeral for one is I
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A television fault, a lecturer and a Welsh region seem jumbled in a broadcasting story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills' puts DON inside SNOWIA, between SNOW and IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdonia is the mountainous national park area of north Wales.

clue.text: Like firm foundation? Anything but

parts.note: a word that looks as if it means resembling bedrock in fact means shaky and unstable

explanation.surface: A remark about a solid base, undercut by a sardonic denial.
explanation.walkthrough: The word seems built from rock plus -y, like solid ground, yet its usual sense is unsteady or troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocky is wobbly or precarious, the opposite of a firm foundation.

clue.text: Tips for youth opening a present carelessly

indicators.note: the tips break open the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: the present moment is now

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters, taken from youth

explanation.surface: A young person tears open a gift without care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips for' takes Y and H from youth; 'opening' sets YH inside A NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anyhow means doing it in a haphazard, slapdash way.

clue.text: Shrub from garland for religious teacher's husband

indicators.note: garland stands in place of husband, so one letter is swapped for the other word

parts.note: the Buddha was the founding religious teacher of Buddhism
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

explanation.surface: Someone takes a shrub as a garland for the husband of a spiritual guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' replaces the H of BUDDHA with LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia is a flowering garden bush, often called the butterfly bush.

clue.text: University backing human rights in case of girl

indicators.note: backing reads the whole assembly from the end to the start
the rights abbreviation sits inside the girl's name as if in a case

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name
HR is the abbreviation for human rights

explanation.surface: A university supports human rights in a case involving a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case of' puts HR inside MAUD, making MAHRUD; 'backing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Durham is a well-known English university city with an old collegiate university.

clue.text: Supported brief suggestion thoroughfare needs repairing?

indicators.note: brief shortens the road word to its familiar abbreviation

parts.note: a street is a thoroughfare, abbreviated St
a road that is rutted is full of furrows and in need of mending

explanation.surface: A terse note backs a proposal that a road needs mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts STREET to ST. Read 'St rutted' as a telegram-style note, a brief suggestion that a road needs mending. 'suggestion' only sets up that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure that is strutted is held up by struts, so it is braced or propped.

clue.text: Computer game, uncomplicated: daughter was about to lose it?

parts.note: a sim is a simulation computer game
mere can mean simple, nothing more than

explanation.surface: A computer game, its simplicity and a daughter on the verge of a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is figurative: someone simmering is close to boiling over with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To simmer is to seethe quietly, close to losing your temper.

clue.text: Insides of pits that scar old island

indicators.note: the insides of each word are the letters left when its ends are dropped

explanation.surface: Pits that leave a scar on an ancient island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insides of' takes IT, HA and CA from pits, that and scar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is the Greek island home of Odysseus in ancient legend.

clue.text: Women's Institute — one's appearing on Thursdays at that

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece coming on another means it follows it

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
Th is the abbreviation for Thursday, so two of them stand for the plural
one's is read as I's, the Roman numeral for one followed by the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute, with someone turning up at its Thursday meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is read as I'S, I for one plus S. Thursdays, plural, gives two abbreviations, TH TH. The WI is a British women's community group.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean thereupon, at that moment, as a sentence opener.

clue.text: Sat before this Bavarian and state guards

indicators.note: guards means the state word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to state is to say
und is German for and, as spoken in Bavaria

explanation.surface: A Bavarian and a state guard someone seated before them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' puts UND inside SAY. 'Sat' is the abbreviation for Saturday, not a past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday comes immediately before the following day of the week, the weekend's second day.

clue.text: Public assembling round green

parts.note: O is round in shape
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A public gathering around a village green.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and done in plain view, as opposed to hidden.

clue.text: One clumsily smothers lines on maps

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: clumsily suggests the letters are handled awkwardly into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily smothers something with lines on maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges SMOTHERS into SOTHERMS, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotherms are lines on weather maps joining places of equal temperature.

clue.text: Appropriate to expose cuts in parts of shipyards

parts.note: fitting means suitable or appropriate
to out someone is to expose them
to dock is to cut short, as with a tail

explanation.surface: It is right to reveal the job cuts at the shipyards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like a verb (take), but it is the adjective, fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting-out docks are where a launched ship is equipped and completed in a yard.

clue.text: Century-old hero finally bagged apple

parts.note: the star of a show is its hero

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of bagged

explanation.surface: An ancient hero finally bags an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes D from bagged.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is an old English variety of large cooking apple.

clue.text: The other corner unknown

parts.note: a nook is a corner
in algebra Y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Something mysterious tucked away in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is British slang for sex, as is nooky.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are coy British slang expressions for sexual activity.

clue.text: Carrier of sound from excellent rock festival venue welcome

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent
IOW is the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast, home of a famous rock festival
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: Something carrying sound from a great rock festival site gets a warm greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight Festival is a long-running British rock festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio waves carry broadcast sound signals through the air.

clue.text: Singular leaves spell colour!

indicators.note: leaves means the abbreviation for singular departs from the other word

parts.note: a stint is a spell of work

explanation.surface: A lone person leaves a spell, exclaiming about colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes S out of STINT. 'Spell' is a period of time, not magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or hue, a light variety of colour.

clue.text: Approach capable of supporting principal

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other, coming after it

parts.note: the lead is the principal role
to be up to something is to be capable of it

explanation.surface: A capable deputy holds up the head of the school.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead up to something is to approach it gradually.

clue.text: With rubber rings worn on the ears?

indicators.note: on the ears means the word is judged by its sound, not spelling

parts.note: worn out means tired

explanation.surface: Something with rubber rings looks worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: TYRED, fitted with tyres, sounds like TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyres are rubber rings on wheels, so a tyred wheel is fitted with them.

clue.text: Band of gold and red's elevated painting

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
Che Guevara was a famous revolutionary red, plus the possessive s

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue lifts the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: A painting of gold and red raised high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns ART upwards to give TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a band of musicians.

clue.text: State of bluegrass in turf from the ground?

indicators.note: the state abbreviation goes inside the turf word

parts.note: sward is an expanse of grass turf
Kentucky, the Bluegrass State, is abbreviated KY

explanation.surface: A patch of Kentucky bluegrass in turf, seen from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts KY inside SWARD. The question mark warns that 'from the ground' describes a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyward means upwards, the direction away from the earth.

clue.text: Hospital department, on hand first to give description of fever?

indicators.note: first says the on and hand pieces come before the hospital department

parts.note: re means on or about
mitt is slang for hand
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A hospital ward, given a hand, writes up a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts RE MITT ahead of ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A remittent fever rises and falls without fully subsiding, a medical term.

clue.text: Not a bit loony left!

definitions.meaning: touched means slightly mad, so not touched is sane
left alone, not handled or interfered with

explanation.definitionFit: Untouched means unaffected or intact, and touched also means slightly crazy.

clue.text: Smoothing things over with girl: one I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Patching things up with a girl I like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges GIRL ONE I. 'Smoothing things over' looks like making peace but means literal lubricating.
explanation.definitionFit: Reoiling is lubricating again, which makes moving parts run smoothly.

clue.text: Chased away, clutching new, smaller sort of gun?

indicators.note: clutching means the chasing phrase holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: saw off means repelled or chased away

explanation.surface: Someone chased off a newcomer with a small gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' puts N inside SAW OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off shotgun has a shortened barrel, so it is smaller.

clue.text: Gorges, maybe, Barnaby's sesame sandwiches

indicators.note: the words sandwich the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Barnaby's sesame sandwiches give him the urge to gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' finds the answer inside barnABY'S SESame.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorges are an example of abysses, deep chasms, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: For all of 7 seconds in stupor, but stirring at eight

indicators.note: seconds means the second letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Someone in a stupor stirs at eight for all of the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to the answer at 7 down, ORCHESTRA. 'seconds in' takes T, U, T, T, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a musical direction meaning all players perform together.

clue.text: Order to carry out: elaborate, briefly

parts.note: to do a task is to carry it out

indicators.note: briefly shortens the word by dropping its final letter

parts.note: rich can mean ornate or elaborate

explanation.surface: A command to carry out, given in brief elaborate terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of RICH, giving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture.

clue.text: Crashed out after eating fine food

indicators.note: after eating means the jumbled word swallows the other piece
crashed means wrecked, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after eating fine food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' rearranges OUT into TOU; 'after eating' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a food made from soya milk.
